mimicry_type.label: Batesian mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A palatable or harmless mimic resembles an unpalatable or dangerous model, deceiving predators that have learned to avoid the model.

mimicry_type.label: Müllerian mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: Two or more defended species converge on a shared warning signal, spreading the cost of predator education among them.

mimicry_type.label: Mertensian mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A more deadly species mimics a less dangerous one, hypothesised to arise when moderately venomous prey benefits from mimicking a milder model.

mimicry_type.label: Aggressive mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A predator or parasite resembles a harmless or attractive signal-bearer to approach its own prey or hosts.

mimicry_type.label: Reproductive mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: Mimicry that exploits the reproductive behaviour of another species, typically by imitating mates or reproductive resources.

mimicry_type.label: Sexual deception
mimicry_type.definition: A mimic imitates the mate or mating signals of its receiver (often chemically and visually) to exploit their mating behaviour, as in pollinator sexual deception.

mimicry_type.label: Brood mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A mimic exploits the parental care of another species, as in brood parasitism where the parasite's offspring are reared by the host.

mimicry_type.label: Egg mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: Mimicry of host eggs by a brood parasite's egg, reducing rejection by the incubating host.

mimicry_type.label: Social mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A mimic infiltrates a social species' colony by imitating its members or their chemical identity.

mimicry_type.label: Parasitic mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A social parasite mimics its host species to gain acceptance inside the host colony or family unit.

mimicry_type.label: Floral mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: A mimic imitates the flowers or floral signals of another species to attract pollinators without offering a reward, or a plant imitates insect signals.

mimicry_type.label: Food deception
mimicry_type.definition: A mimic imitates food or food-related signals to exploit the foraging behaviour of receivers.

mimicry_type.label: Protective mimicry
mimicry_type.definition: Mimicry in which the mimic gains protection from predation or aggression by resembling something the receiver avoids or ignores.

mimicry_type.label: Automimicry
mimicry_type.definition: Within one species, palatable individuals or body parts resemble unpalatable ones, so the receiver cannot distinguish them.

mimicry_type.label: Masquerade
mimicry_type.definition: A mimic prevents recognition as prey by resembling an inedible object or organism of no interest to the receiver, rather than a warning signal.

mimicry_type.label: Uncertain
mimicry_type.definition: The mimicry interpretation is unclear or contested — recorded with the dispute visible.

mimicry_type.label: Other
mimicry_type.definition: A mimicry pattern that does not fit the established categories.

model_kind.label: Environment or background (foliage, bark, sand, water)

system_type.label: Species complex centred on one lineage
